facts_of_case: The respondent/wife filed a petition under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for restitution of conjugal rights. The trial court allowed the petition after recording statements of both parties. The husband is aggrieved by this order and has filed an appeal.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking a decree under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, has to plead and prove by evidence that the other spouse has withdrawn from his/her society without reasonable excuse.
legal_principles.held: Any party seeking a decree under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, has to plead and prove by evidence that the other spouse has withdrawn from his/her society without reasonable excuse and the Court on being satisfied of the veracity of the statements made in such petition and that there is no legal ground why the application should not be granted, may decree restitution of conjugal rights accordingly.

legal_principles.principle: The burden of proving the reason for withdrawal from the society of another lies with the person who has withdrawn.
legal_principles.held: Section 9 further provides that where a question arises whether there has been a reasonable excuse for withdrawal from the society of another, the burden of proving the same shall lie with the person who has withdrawn from the society of the other.

outcome.final_order: Delay in filing appeal condoned, application disposed of.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
preparing an appeal against an order of restitution of conjugal rights
conducting a matrimonial dispute in Family Court
